{\scriptsize\textit{Notes:} North America, vintages up to 2010, single-factor $\hat\beta_{MKT}$ (Bartlett sandwich SE, $S=\lceil1.3\sqrt V\rceil$). L2$-U_{v,H}$: for Buyout ($V=25$ for both estimators), full-sample difference with leave-one-vintage-out (LOO) jackknife SE in parentheses (fixed full-sample domain); for VC ($V=27$ full vs.\ $V=23$ eligible $n_v\ge2$ vintages), full-sample difference followed in brackets by the matched-vintage difference on the same 23 vintages (matched L2 estimates, jackknife SEs, and matched AR sets are recorded in \texttt{iv\_comparison\_rows.csv}). Expected gap: paired mean L2 minus $U_{v,H}$ difference in the data-shaped core Monte Carlo without vintage-level effects (EW: \texttt{core\_BO/VC}; FW: \texttt{s\_core\_BO/VC} at 0 and 15 yr), MC SE in parentheses. IV roots: all zeros of $V^{-1}\sum_v z_v PV_v(\beta)=0$ ($z_v=A_{v,H}(1)/A_{v,0}(1)$, $z_v=1$ at $H=0$) on the admissible domain; LOO no-root: share of delete-one-vintage refits on the fixed full-sample domain that lose every root (zero-root refits are never replaced by squared-moment minimizers). Nominal 95\% AR set: acceptance region from inverting the centered Bartlett fixed-$b$ moment test (scores $s_v(\beta)-\bar s(\beta)$, $S=\lceil1.3\sqrt V\rceil$, $b=S/V$, critical values 2.790 for $V=25$ and 2.722 for $V=27$), avoiding root selection and weak-slope division. Calibration caveat: robustness to roots and coverage under finite-$V$ persistence are distinct properties---at true $\beta=1$, this moment test rejects 4.0\%/3.4\% in independent BO/VC cores, 9.4\%/11.1\% under persistent M4 ($c/2c$, $\rho_W=0.6$), and 19.2\%/8.8\% ($c$) and 21.8\%/9.8\% ($2c$) in Design~A$'$ ($V=25/100$), so the sets are reported as a nominal, calibrated-by-design diagnostic. $^\dagger$: estimate on a bound of $\Theta$, no SE.}
